### Verse 5

The eye of the sacrifice, the beginning, and the face, I offer with speech, with hearing, and with the mind.
May the gods, being well-disposed, come to this sacrifice spread out by the All-Maker <note>original: "Vishvakarman"</note>.

#### Word-for-word analysis
The sacrifice’s. Eye. Beginning. Face. And. With speech. With hearing. With mind. I offer.
This. Sacrifice. Spread out. By the All-Maker. [Towards]. Gods. May they come. Being well-disposed.

#### Commentary
This verse has been explained previously <note>referencing Atharva Veda 2.35.5</note>. I offer the senses such as the eye and the mind in connection with the sacrifice; I make them devoted to it. The summary meaning is: may the gods, acting with a favorable mind, come to this mental sacrifice which is extended and spread out by the God who is the creator of all, the All-Maker.

### Verse 6

Those who are the priests of the gods and those who are worthy of sacrifice, to whom the sacrificial portion is made an offering.
Coming to this sacrifice along with their wives, may all the gods, being powerful, rejoice.

#### Word-for-word analysis
Those. Of the gods. Priests. Those. And. Worthy of sacrifice. For whom. Offering. Is made. Apportionment.
This. Sacrifice. With. Wives. Having come. However many. Gods. Powerful. May they rejoice.

#### Commentary
Among the gods, those who are priests <note>original: "rtvijah"</note> are those who sacrifice at the proper time. And those who are worthy of sacrifice are those to whom the sacrifice is offered. For both types of gods, the offering is made as their assigned portion. However many gods there are, may all those great and powerful gods come to this sacrifice along with their respective wives, such as Indrani and others, and may they be satisfied by accepting the offering.

This concludes the fourth hymn in the seventh section <note>original: "anuvaka"</note>.

### Introduction to the next Hymn
